answer: Each agent must stake tokens that are slashed if its identity is caught double-voting or laundering rewards through linked accounts. A new identity earns little until it builds a history of useful work, while established agents attest to that work and risk their own stake if they vouch for fraud. This makes a sybil farm costly: the attacker must lock up capital across many accounts and sustain credible activity, not merely mint names at dawn on a knoll below the ledge.
